Across 19 eligible m≤20, scanned the full coefficient box, including nonprimitive triples, plus a separate monic scan. The six positive-leading minima at m=5,11 and four elsewhere matched the list.
correctness.rationale: For squarefree d=4m(m+1)−1 and m≥1, the field discriminant is −d. Scaling a root by A yields an integral generator with discriminant −dt², for a nonzero integral index t. Thus 4AC≥d>4m² and the displayed polynomial attains m+1. At that cap d>(m+1)² forces |t|=1, B is odd, and AC≥m(m+1) forces each positive coefficient A,C to be at least m. The three remaining pairs give B²=1 or 4m+5; the latter also requires |B|≤m+1. Changing overall sign covers negative leading coefficients. For monic polynomials the norm of u+vω is ((2u+v)²+dv²)/4: when |v|=1 the odd trace has magnitude at least one, and |v|≥2 gives a strictly larger norm. The element ω attains the monic minimum, giving the ratio m. The quadratic has nonzero discriminant and no fixed square divisor (already f(0)=−1), so the classical quadratic squarefree-value theorem applies.
residual_risks: The finite check does not establish density or uniformity; these follow from the proof and the classical theorem. No statement about nonsquarefree d, or infinite occurrence of the symmetric exception, follows.

value.rationale: The family lies just above the previous integral discriminant-height cap and realizes the sharp next cap. Classifying all ways to attain it identifies precisely when the generic four positive-leading optimizers gain two symmetric exceptions, information a height bound cannot give. The exact comparison with monic coefficients isolates the cost of requiring integral generators on the same family. Value rests on this complete equality classification, not on another proof of discriminant bounds, density or unboundedness alone.
